key_insight: UNSM-treated Cr₃C₂–NiCr coatings showed sample-dependent hardness, with different treatment settings producing the highest values for detonation-sprayed and HVOF deposits.
engineering_relevance: UNSM settings should be evaluated separately for each deposition route, considering both local hardness and surface integrity.
method: Evaluated four UNSM-treated samples per deposition route: detonation spray and HVOF.
Applied static loads of 20 or 30 N and vibration amplitudes of 20 or 30 µm.
Measured instrumental hardness at 300 mN with a 10 s dwell and examined post-scratch surfaces by SEM.
evidence_signal: Hardness ranged from 820–970 HV for detonation-sprayed coatings and 546–1165 HV for HVOF coatings, peaking at 20 N/20 µm and 30 N/30 µm, respectively.
watch_item: Post-scratch SEM observations do not isolate UNSM-induced damage or establish a scratch-resistance ranking.
paper_title: HARDNESS AND POST-SCRATCH SURFACE MORPHOLOGY OF Cr₃C₂–NiCr COATINGS AFTER ULTRASONIC NANOCRYSTAL SURFACE MODIFICATION
